title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 281
paragraphs: Of the animals that live with men there are great numbers, and would be many more but for the accidents that befall the cats. When the females have produced young they no longer resort to the males, and the males, seeking to be united with them, cannot. To this end, then, they contrive as follows: they either take away by force or remove secretly the young from the females and kill them (but after killing they do not eat them); and the females, deprived of their young and still desiring more, come therefore to the males, for the cat is a creature fond of its young. Moreover, when a fire occurs, the cats seem to be divinely possessed; for while the Egyptians stand at intervals and look after the cats, taking no care to extinguish the fire, the cats slip between the men or leap over them and jump into the fire; and when this happens, great mourning comes upon the Egyptians. In whatever houses a cat has died by a natural death, all who live in that house shave only their eyebrows; but in whatever houses a dog has died, they shave their whole body and head.
